interpretation: A factor of two in the cross-section - which is a factor of only sqrt(2) in the kinetic diameter - moves the supported endpoint from 170.0 km to between 155.0 and 190.0 km. The endpoint is a declared-bracket boundary, not a measured transition altitude, and this is the size of the declaration's influence on it.
method: Kn = lambda/L with lambda = 1/(sqrt(2) n sigma), so Kn is exactly inversely proportional to sigma at fixed density and length. Scaling sigma by f is read off the stored profile as scaling every Kn by 1/f. No model is run and no new quantity is computed.
question: How far does the supported endpoint move under a factor-two error in the collision cross-section?
what_this_does_not_establish: Nothing about the true cross-sections. A factor of two is a plausible span for hard-sphere surrogates against real collision integrals; it is not an error bar, because no reference set was available to form one against.
